item.text: {"case_id":"SPR00044","decision":"candidate","candidate_ranking":["C15","C11","C20"],"selected_candidate_label":"C15","confidence":0.99,"relationship_type":"both","rationale":"C15 is a direct drafting precursor. The child repeats its distinctive operative formula suspending all legal provisions requiring professional examinations for promotion in the Regular Army's Medical, Dental, and Veterinary Corps, while expanding coverage to analogous Air Force officers and replacing the fixed expiration date with the duration of the 1950 national emergency. C11 and C20 also concern emergency suspensions of legal requirements, but their shared machinery is less specific and concerns the eight-hour law rather than professional promotion examinations.","shared_material":[{"child_excerpt":"The operation of all provisions of law requiring professional examinations for promotion in the Regular Army of officers of the Medical, Dental, and Veterinary Corps ... are hereby suspended","parent_excerpt":"The operation of all provisions of law requiring professional examinations for permanent promotion in the Regular Army of officers of the Medical, Dental, and Veterinary Corps is hereby suspended","explanation":"This is nearly verbatim, distinctive operative language covering the same examinations, promotion process, service, and officer corps."},{"child_excerpt":"and in the United States Air Force of officers designated as medical, dental, and veterinary officers thereof","parent_excerpt":"in the Regular Army of officers of the Medical, Dental, and Veterinary Corps","explanation":"The child adapts the parent's covered-personnel structure by adding equivalent Air Force medical categories."},{"child_excerpt":"for the duration of the national emergency proclaimed by [DIRECTIVE_REFERENCE] of December 16, 1950","parent_excerpt":"until June 30, 1948","explanation":"Both provisions use the same suspension mechanism but substitute a new duration tied to the later national emergency."}]}
